summary: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO is today's clearest gap story — Memeburn covered the stock drop and the AG subpoena but not today's reinstatement — alongside a genuinely new Anthropic agent launch (Claude Ship) and a practical iPhone/crypto malware warning (MoldyRoost) worth a protect-yourself piece. Phone news is thin on big launches today, so the 70%-phone slate leans on leak roundups, one comparison pick (Kodak SlideTag vs. AirTag), and smaller confirmed stories rather than forcing weak filler. Reddit crawl failed (403, one of several sources) but coverage elsewhere is unaffected; nothing cleared the bar for 'breaking' given the Nvidia story's 2-hour window has passed and its sensitivity calls for care over speed.

topics.working_title: Jensen Huang is Nvidia's CEO again — what changed in 48 hours
topics.why_now: Reinstated Nov 23 after reported Trump/Vance pressure on Nvidia's board (Techmeme via Axios/Reuters); Nasdaq 100 jumped 7%, CoreWeave +22%, Tesla +11% same day (Techmeme/Bloomberg); Hacker News front page at 2,019 points/3,093 comments; the Commerce Department simultaneously added Megaspeed — the company tied to Huang's scandal — to its entity list. Memeburn covered the stock drop (Nov 21) and the AG subpoena (Nov 22) but not today's reinstatement.
topics.angle: Lead with the business mechanics — stock reaction, board governance, chip-export fallout — rather than the affair/scandal details other outlets are already leading with; own the 'what this means for Nvidia and AI chip supply' angle.

topics.working_title: A single tap can drain your crypto wallet on an unpatched iPhone
topics.why_now: CoinDesk and Cointelegraph both detail the MoldyRoost campaign: 480+ ad domains across 47+ countries, with researchers stating that just loading the landing page on a vulnerable iPhone (iOS 18 or earlier) is enough to get infected. The US is among the affected countries — exactly the practical 'is this safe / how do I protect myself' search pattern that performs for Memeburn.
topics.angle: Make it a straight protect-yourself piece: who's at risk (anyone on iOS 18 or earlier who taps the wrong ad), what the exploit actually steals (wallet seed phrases from notes/photos), and the concrete fixes — update iOS, stop storing seed phrases as screenshots, use a hardware wallet.
headline_options: This iPhone Ad Scam Can Steal Your Crypto With One Tap
MoldyRoost: The iPhone Malvertising Campaign Draining Crypto Wallets
Is Your iPhone Safe From MoldyRoost? What to Check Right Now

sources.title: Crypto thieves are using online ads to infect iPhones with a single tap, research finds
'MoldyRoost' ads can steal crypto wallet recovery phrases from iPhones

topics.notes_for_writer: Confirmed via source read: exploit targets iOS 18 and earlier (not the latest iOS); heaviest targeting is Hong Kong/Japan/Singapore but US users are also affected — don't overstate US-specific risk, but the fix (update iOS, don't screenshot seed phrases) applies to every reader.
